items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: We had the band with Lou Marini, Alan Rubin, Howard Johnson, Paul Shaffer... The horn section was Alan Rubin, Lou Marini, Tom Scott, and myself.

ctx.x: Wow. I mean that’s paying some dues. And I wonder, this is — I wasn’t going to go here yet but the current music student that now, at the age you were then, how do they pay dues?

Well the whole music scene, the professional music scene, has drastically changed in New York and LA. I can tell you more about New York. When I got to New York in 1970, January 1970, every TV show had a big band. All three networks had over a hundred musicians on staff getting a weekly check. That doesn’t exist anymore. And I have to say that the Saturday Night Live band that we started in 1975 was the first non- big band network TV show. And from then on every new network TV show followed our cue — instead of a…

When you were writing for them and for bands with horns, a lot of times like let’s say you had trumpet, tenor and trombone. What — is your voicing you’d think, well obviously the trumpet’s going to be on the top and the tenor’s going to go in the middle and the trombone’s on the bottom. Is that true?
